title: Gaze, consider, contemplate, imitate (Clare to Agnes)
hookLine: Clare's four steps before the crucified Christ
tomorrow: how many ways are there to water a garden?

cards: Self-improvement plans usually start with doing: a new routine, a tracker, a list of habits. A letter from Assisi starts somewhere else.
Clare, who lived with her sisters at San Damiano, writes to Agnes of Prague, a princess who chose the same poor life. Partway through, Clare sends four verbs in a row, like four steps on a stair.
And the first one isn't do. It's look.

teach.b: The question is old: where does a changed life begin? Clare answers with an order. First, gaze.
Look at Christ, poor and crucified, the one who made himself lowly for your sake. Not study yet. Just look.
Second, consider. The looking slows down and starts to notice: who is this, and what did he choose? Third, contemplate.
The noticing goes quiet, and the heart rests on what it has seen. Fourth, imitate, and here's the turn.
Clare writes it as a longing: as you desire to imitate him. The doing grows out of the looking. Muslims have a neighbor teaching on where worship begins.

teach.h: IHSAN: AS THOUGH YOU SEE HIM.
teach.b: In a hadith found in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, the angel Gabriel asks the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, about ihsan, excellence in faith.
He answers: to worship God as though you see Him, and if you don't see Him, He sees you. Both put seeing at the start: a life shaped by attention to God.
The honest difference: Clare's gaze rests on Christ crucified, God seen in a human face, and Catholics pray before images of him.
In Islam God is not pictured at all; the seeing is of the heart, and the hadith ends on being seen.

how: Catholics pray before the crucifix and holy images, and the Poor Clares, the order that grew from Clare's community, still read her letters to Agnes.

o: a nun's vow to keep her eyes lowered
looking at Christ before doing anything
staring at something until you go blank

games.q: clare's four steps — tap the pairs.
p: look at Christ, poor and crucified
the heart rests on what it saw
worship as though you see God

s: Clare tells Agnes to begin by trying harder
she begins with the eyes: gaze, consider, contemplate.
Clare writes the fourth step, imitate, as a desire rather than an order
as you desire to imitate him: the doing grows from the looking.
in the hadith of Gabriel, ihsan means worshiping God as though you see Him
and if you don't see Him, He sees you.

games.q: your cousin wants to become more patient and has a month-long plan with an app and a tracker. what would Clare suggest first?
o: look first: spend time gazing at the one you'd like to be like.
start the tracker today; doing has to come before anything else.
wait until patience shows up on its own, then begin.
games.why: Clare starts with the eyes: gaze, consider, contemplate. imitating comes last, and as a longing that grows out of the looking.

practice: Choose one thing to look at: a crucifix, an icon, a picture of Christ, or, if you have none, an image of someone giving themselves for others. Take Clare's steps slowly: gaze, then consider, then contemplate.
Let the fourth, imitate, stay a quiet wish for now.

wordCard.voice: Gaze. The first of Clare's four steps: look at Christ before trying to do anything at all.

orig.note: Latin for gaze: the first of the four verbs in Clare's second letter to Agnes.

carryVoice: Your line: gaze. For Clare, the doing grows out of the looking, never the other way round. See you tomorrow.
